video_title: Jayson Tatum vs. Jaylen Brown: Is it beef or is it nothing? 🤔 | Big Day with Peter Schrager

quotes.speaker: Jayson Tatum
quotes.summary_phrase: Jayson Tatum denies any personal beef with Jaylen Brown
quotes.excerpt: It's no beef or it's not about that. It should be more about praise.
quotes.quote: There are many people playing in this league who never went to the finals. We went twice and won a championship, so it should be more about that. There is no beef or it's not about that. It's not about Shaq and Kobe. There is no beef. I don't, it's not about that. It should be more about, you know, praise and, you know, I understand that doesn't necessarily sell and drama gets clicks and views, but I'm not really into that. That's not my thing.

quotes.speaker: Jaylen Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Jaylen Brown addresses his comments on Jayson Tatum
quotes.excerpt: There's no beef, but it might be a little lamb chops and some gravy.
quotes.quote: There's no beef. Jayson comes from a wonderful family. We've accomplished some great things. He's a hell of a basketball player. He's got a great PR team. There's no beef, but you know, it might be a little lamb chops and some gravy. You know what I mean? You should stay ready at all times. There's no beef. It should never ever be that. It's just basketball. We both blessed, but it might be a little lamb chop, it'll be all right.

quotes.speaker: Steve Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Smith analyzes the competitive nature of Tatum and Brown
quotes.excerpt: It is straight up what he said. It's not beef. It's great PR team.

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Smith
text_blocks.text: The damn grill is so fired up and it is ready to barbecue whatever is going to be thrown on the grill. And I'm going to tell you what ain't thrown on the grill: ain't no fish, it ain't no planks. It is straight up what he said. It's not beef. It's great PR team. You got one guy who ain't about that life and you got another guy who he said, be ready, stay ready. That means I'm going to pull up, and when I pull up, stay less.

text_blocks.speaker: Steve Smith
text_blocks.text: It's ego, man. It's ego, but competitiveness. So you're going to be competitive. That means on the court, when I high-five, when I, oh, we're former champs, let's hug and embrace, no, it's like, hey, you better bring your A-game, because I'm coming at you. If I get an opportunity to dunk on you, I will. If I get an opportunity to steal a ball, give you an extra little, you know, throw a little hot sauce on that chicken wing, then I'll do that.

quotes.speaker: Steve Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Steve Smith explains the competitive tension between Tatum and Brown
quotes.excerpt: These are two superstars who one believes he was wronged in his exit.
quotes.quote: These are two superstars who one believes he was wronged in his exit and another guy is playing the, I don't know what happened, I'm just as shocked as you. That's the part in the competitive sports that you go, stop. I mean, you got to say, okay, when I see you, we might have to have a talk because this I didn't know came out of the blue. I could tell you as being a guy on the team, when they were key players on the team, I had the opportunity to call, like, yo, what are we doing? Are we really getting rid of this person? Well, how is that helping me? So you have that kind of conversation with management. So to say that he had no idea, I disagree just a lot.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst compares the Celtics-Sixers dynamic to grade school
quotes.excerpt: NBA basketball, if you can get rid of the money, is very similar to grade school basketball.
quotes.quote: NBA basketball, if you can get rid of the money, is very similar to grade school basketball, and this is a grade school situation. The guy who didn't get sent off thinks everything should be fine. The guy who did get sent off says it ain't fine, and they're both determined to live their life better to prove the other guy wrong.

quotes.speaker: Mike Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Mike Brown critiques the Knicks' performance after a loss
quotes.excerpt: Our crap stinks. You know, it does. And we're the only ones that can do something about it.
quotes.quote: Our crap stinks. You know, it does. And we're the only ones that can do something about it. There's no light switch that we can just turn on and think we're going to go win ball games. Nobody's going to give us anything. So we have to be better with the little things until we start shooting the ball well.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Brian Windhorst identifies the Knicks' offensive struggles
quotes.excerpt: Their offense is 29th a week into the season. You've got Jaylen Brunson in a slump.
quotes.quote: If you want to look at the big blinking situation, it's their offense. Their offense is 29th a week into the season. You've got Jaylen Brunson in a slump. Mikal Bridges can't hit anything. Carl Towns, we saw routinely getting six or seven assists in those playoff games last year, he's averaging two assists a game right now. Look, last year the Chicago Bulls started the year 5-0 and nobody ever thought that was going to last. 0-3 is not going to last, but they can start getting their crap not stinking so much by doing a little bit better on offense.
